# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.  Waterbirds experiment implementation (full 30 epochs)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

def run_waterbirds() -> None:
    """Runs EXP-1 with 5 seeds and all baselines, saves CSV & figures."""

    # 7.1 Download / load dataset – fails loudly if totally unavailable
    try:
        wb = get_dataset("waterbirds", version="2.0", root_dir=str(DATA_DIR), download=True)
    except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
        print("[bold red]FATAL:[/] Waterbirds v2 could not be downloaded → abort.")
        raise exc

    n_groups = wb.n_groups

    # 7.2 loaders (shared transforms already defined)
    def make_loader(split: str, batch_size: int, shuffle: bool):
        return get_train_loader("standard" if split == "train" else "evaluation",
                                 wb,
                                 split=split,
                                 batch_size=batch_size,
                                 num_workers=4,
                                 transform=train_tf_wb if split == "train" else val_tf_wb)

    # 7.3 model factory (ResNet-50-In21k)
    def build_model() -> nn.Module:
        m = create_model("resnetv2_50x1_bit.goog_in21k_ft_in1k", pretrained=True)
        m.reset_classifier(num_classes=wb.n_classes)
        return m.to(DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE)

    # 7.4 bookkeeping
    rows = []

    for seed in WB_SEEDS:
        set_seed(seed)
        loaders = {s: make_loader(s, 128, s == "train") for s in ("train", "val")}

        # build SINGLE backbone per seed (weights shared to all methods for fairness)
        backbone_sd = build_model().state_dict()

        for method in [
            "ERM", "IRM", "REx", "GroupDRO", "DFR", "AutoSpuSwap", "swap0",
        ]:
            model = build_model()
            model.load_state_dict(backbone_sd)  # identical init
            optimiser = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=3e-4, weight_decay=0.05)
            scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR(optimiser, T_max=30)

            # GroupDRO helper
            if method == "GroupDRO":
                gdro_helper = GroupDROLoss(n_groups)

            autospu = None
            irm = None
            rex = None
            if method.startswith("AutoSpuSwap"):
                autospu = AutoSpuSwapModule(1.0 if method == "AutoSpuSwap" else 0.0, 1.0, 0.3)
            elif method == "IRM":
                irm = IRMLoss(1_000.0)
            elif method == "REx":
                rex = RExLoss(10.0)

            # ───────────── training loop (30 epochs) ─────────────
            for epoch in range(30):
                model.train()
                metric_log = defaultdict(list)
                for batch in loaders["train"]:
                    x, y, g, _ = batch["images"], batch["y"], batch["metadata"][:, 0], batch["metadata"]
                    x, y, g = x.to(DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE), y.to(DEVICE), g.to(DEVICE)

                    optimiser.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
                    with AMP_CONTEXT(device_type=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE):
                        if autospu is not None:
                            loss, extra = autospu(model, x, y)
                        else:
                            logits = model(x)
                            if irm is not None:
                                loss = irm(logits, y)
                            elif rex is not None:
                                # assume two environments per batch – split half/half
                                loss_envs = [F.cross_entropy(logits[i :: 2], y[i :: 2]) for i in (0, 1)]
                                loss = rex(loss_envs)
                            elif method == "GroupDRO":
                                # compute per-group loss
                                group_losses = torch.zeros(n_groups, device=DEVICE)
                                for gid in range(n_groups):
                                    idx = g == gid
                                    if idx.any():
                                        group_losses[gid] = F.cross_entropy(
                                            logits[idx], y[idx]
                                        )
                                loss = gdro_helper.update(group_losses)
                            else:  # ERM / DFR / swap0
                                loss = F.cross_entropy(logits, y)

                    loss.backward()
                    optimiser.step()

                    metric_log["loss"].append(loss.detach().cpu())
                    if autospu is not None:
                        metric_log["Δlogits"].append(extra["Δlogits"].cpu())
                scheduler.step()
                # quick val every 5 epochs to monitor
                if (epoch + 1) % 5 == 0:
                    val_acc, val_wg = eval_waterbirds(model, loaders["val"], n_groups)
                    print(
                        f"seed{seed} [{method}] epoch{epoch+1:02d}  val-acc={val_acc:.2%}  WG={val_wg:.2%}"
                    )

            # ───────────── end of training – full eval on val ─────────────
            logits_all, y_all, g_all = [], [], []
            model.eval()
            for batch in loaders["val"]:
                x, y, g = batch["images"].to(DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE), batch["y"].to(DEVICE), batch["metadata"][:, 0].to(DEVICE)
                with AMP_CONTEXT(device_type=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE):
                    logits = model(x)
                logits_all.append(logits.cpu())
                y_all.append(y.cpu())
                g_all.append(g.cpu())
            logits_all = torch.cat(logits_all)
            y_all = torch.cat(y_all)
            g_all = torch.cat(g_all)
            pred_all = logits_all.argmax(1)
            id_acc = (pred_all == y_all).float().mean().item()
            wg_acc = compute_wg_acc(pred_all, y_all, g_all, n_groups)
            ece = expected_calibration_error(logits_all, y_all)

            row = {
                "seed": seed,
                "method": method,
                "id_acc": id_acc,
                "wg_acc": wg_acc,
                "ece": ece,
            }
            rows.append(row)

            # save checkpoint for seed 0 (large file – keep one per method)
            if seed == 0:
                torch.save(model.state_dict(), CKPT_DIR / f"wb_{method.lower()}.pt")

        # ───────────── DFR post-hoc linear probe (needs group labels) ─────────────
        # Fit on balanced val set
        dfr_rows = [r for r in rows if r["seed"] == seed and r["method"] == "DFR"]
        if dfr_rows:
            # extract penultimate layer features – last conv avg-pool output
            model = build_model()
            model.load_state_dict(torch.load(CKPT_DIR / "wb_erm.pt"))  # use ERM features
            model.eval()
            feats, labels = [], []
            for batch in loaders["train"]:
                x, y = batch["images"].to(DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE), batch["y"].numpy()
                with torch.no_grad(), AMP_CONTEXT(device_type=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE):
                    feat = model.forward_features(x).cpu().numpy()
                    feats.append(feat)
                    labels.append(y)
            feats = np.concatenate(feats)
            labels = np.concatenate(labels)
            lin = LogisticRegression(max_iter=200).fit(feats, labels)
            # evaluate on val
            feats_val, labels_val, groups_val = [], [], []
            for batch in loaders["val"]:
                x, y, g = batch["images"], batch["y"], batch["metadata"][:, 0]
                with torch.no_grad(), AMP_CONTEXT(device_type=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE):
                    feat = model.forward_features(x.to(DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE)).cpu().numpy()
                feats_val.append(feat)
                labels_val.append(y.numpy())
                groups_val.append(g.numpy())
            feats_val = np.concatenate(feats_val)
            labels_val = np.concatenate(labels_val)
            groups_val = np.concatenate(groups_val)
            pred_val = lin.predict(feats_val)
            id_acc = (pred_val == labels_val).mean()
            wg_acc = min((pred_val[groups_val == gid] == labels_val[groups_val == gid]).mean() for gid in range(n_groups))
            rows.append({"seed": seed, "method": "DFR-eval", "id_acc": id_acc, "wg_acc": wg_acc, "ece": np.nan})

    # 7.5 aggregate stats & paired t-test
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df.to_csv(RESULTS_DIR / f"{EXP_TAG_WB}.csv", index=False)

    means = df.groupby("method")["id_acc", "wg_acc"].mean()
    stds = df.groupby("method")["id_acc", "wg_acc"].std()
    print("\n[bold]Waterbirds summary (val split after 30 epochs):[/]")
    print(pd.concat([means, stds.rename(columns=lambda c: c + "_std")], axis=1))

    # paired t-test AutoSpuSwap vs best baseline (GroupDRO)
    autospu = df[df.method == "AutoSpuSwap"]["wg_acc"]
    best_base = df[df.method == "GroupDRO"]["wg_acc"]
    t_stat, p_val = ttest_rel(autospu, best_base)
    print(f"Paired t-test AutoSpuSwap vs GroupDRO:  t={t_stat:.2f}  p={p_val:.4f}")

    # 7.6  Figures (training curves already printed epoch-wise; here final bar)
    save_bar(means["wg_acc"], "worst_group_accuracy.pdf", ylabel="WG-Acc (%)", multiply=100)


# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 8.  Evaluation helper (shared by WB + diagnostics)
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def eval_waterbirds(model: nn.Module, loader, n_groups: int):  # noqa: ANN001
    model.eval()
    y_cat, g_cat, pred_cat, logits_cat = [], [], [], []
    for batch in loader:
        x, y, g = batch["images"].to(DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE), batch["y"].to(DEVICE), batch["metadata"][:, 0].to(DEVICE)
        with AMP_CONTEXT(device_type=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE):
            logits = model(x)
        pred = logits.argmax(1)
        y_cat.append(y)
        g_cat.append(g)
        pred_cat.append(pred)
        logits_cat.append(logits)
    y_cat = torch.cat(y_cat)
    g_cat = torch.cat(g_cat)
    pred_cat = torch.cat(pred_cat)
    logits_cat = torch.cat(logits_cat)
    id_acc = (pred_cat == y_cat).float().mean().item()
    wg_acc = compute_wg_acc(pred_cat, y_cat, g_cat, n_groups)
    return id_acc, wg_acc

def save_bar(series: pd.Series, fname: str, ylabel: str, multiply: float = 1.0) -> None:  # noqa: D401
    plt.figure(figsize=(4, 2.5))
    bars = plt.bar(range(len(series)), series.values * multiply, tick_label=series.index, color="steelblue")
    for bar in bars:
        h = bar.get_height()
        plt.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, h, f"{h:.1f}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7)
    plt.ylabel(ylabel)
    plt.tight_layout()
    fig_path = FIG_DIR / fname
    plt.savefig(fig_path, format="pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close()
    print("Saved figure:", fig_path)

def run_diagnostics():
    """Runs invariance diagnostics on saved checkpoints."""
    print("\n[bold cyan]Running invariance diagnostics …[/]")
    # load ERM and AutoSpuSwap checkpoints (seed0) – must exist
    erm = create_model("resnetv2_50x1_bit.goog_in21k_ft_in1k", pretrained=False)
    erm.load_state_dict(torch.load(CKPT_DIR / "wb_erm.pt", map_location="cpu"))
    auto = create_model("resnetv2_50x1_bit.goog_in21k_ft_in1k", pretrained=False)
    auto.load_state_dict(torch.load(CKPT_DIR / "wb_autospuswap.pt", map_location="cpu"))
    erm, auto = erm.to(DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE), auto.to(DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE)

    wb = get_dataset("waterbirds", version="2.0", root_dir=str(DATA_DIR), download=False)
    val_loader = get_eval_loader("standard", wb, split="val", batch_size=64, num_workers=2, transform=val_tf_wb)

    # Δlogits(orig, cf)  + label semantics via CLIP (approx.)
    swapper = ContextSwapper(1.0)
    deltas_erm, deltas_auto, sem_change = [], [], 0
    try:
        import clip

        clip_model, clip_pre = clip.load("ViT-B/32", device=DEVICE)
    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover – CLIP optional
        clip_model = clip_pre = None

    with torch.no_grad():
        for batch in val_loader:
            x, y = batch["images"].to(DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE), batch["y"].to(DEVICE)
            x_cf, _ = swapper(x, y)
            if clip_model is not None:
                # CLIP expects float32 0-1 scaled 224×224
                def clip_encode(img):
                    img = (img.float().cpu() - torch.tensor(IMNET_MEAN)[None, :, None, None]) / torch.tensor(IMNET_STD)[
                        None, :, None, None
                    ]
                    img = clip_pre.transforms(img)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
                    return clip_model.encode_image(img.to(DEVICE))

                sem_change += (clip_encode(x).argmax(1) != clip_encode(x_cf).argmax(1)).float().sum().item()
            logits_e = erm(x)
            logits_e_cf = erm(x_cf)
            logits_a = auto(x)
            logits_a_cf = auto(x_cf)
            deltas_erm.append((logits_e - logits_e_cf).pow(2).mean(1).sqrt())
            deltas_auto.append((logits_a - logits_a_cf).pow(2).mean(1).sqrt())
    delta_erm = torch.cat(deltas_erm).mean().item()
    delta_auto = torch.cat(deltas_auto).mean().item()
    sem_preserved = 1 - sem_change / len(val_loader.dataset)

    # WG-Acc gap for swap_prob sweep is done during training grid – skipped here

    diag = {
        "Δlogits_ERM": delta_erm,
        "Δlogits_AutoSpuSwap": delta_auto,
        "semantics_preserved": sem_preserved,
    }
    with open(RESULTS_DIR / f"{EXP_TAG_DIAG}.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(diag, f, indent=2)
    print("Diagnostics saved →", RESULTS_DIR / f"{EXP_TAG_DIAG}.json")

consistency_feedback:
Major internal mismatches prevent the current results from supporting the paper’s claims.

1. Core method not executed
   • The run log shows that the AutoSpuSwap module falls back to an identity (no-op) wrapper (“pipeline not yet implemented – falling back to identity counter-factuals”).  All counterfactual, Fourier and re-weighting steps that constitute the contribution are therefore absent.  Reported gains (+25 pp WG-Acc, −15 % mCE, etc.) cannot arise from the code that actually ran.

2. Key metrics missing
   • Worst-group accuracy, the central metric for Waterbirds, is never computed; only overall validation accuracy is printed.
   • Experiments #2 and #3 are only described; no numeric results from code execution are provided.

3. Dataset/count inconsistencies
   • Config states Waterbirds train=3 495 images, but the HuggingFace loader produces 4 795.  This contradicts both the methods section and the split sizes used in prior work, making comparisons unreliable.

4. Baseline parity not ensured
   • GroupDRO, DFR, etc. are listed but not trained in the run.  Without identical training schedules the claimed relative improvements are speculative.

5. Single-seed reporting
   • Only one seed is run although five are promised; variability and statistical confidence are therefore unknown.

6. Requirements vs. hardware realism
   • requirements.txt pulls CUDA 12 wheels, but the manuscript states experiments are on a single NVIDIA T4 (CUDA 11.8).  Version skew can change performance and hinders exact replication.

Actionable steps to reach high consistency (score ≥ 8)
1. Implement and verify each pipeline component (mask discovery, context swap, Fourier perturbation, last-layer reweighting).  Add unit tests that fail if the identity fall-back is accidentally used.
2. Compute and log all declared metrics (ID-Acc, WG-Acc, mCE, held-out-domain acc) for every method and seed; store them in CSV/JSON for easy inspection.
3. Align dataset splits with prior work (3 495/349/5794) or clearly justify new splits; if HF loader differs, script an exact replication of the original split file.
4. Run all baselines under the exact same training schedule and hardware; include standard deviation over ≥3 seeds and perform paired t-tests to show significance.
5. Provide full results for Experiments #2 and #3, or drop claims until code is available.
6. Add a sanity check: if context swapping is disabled, WG-Acc should regress toward ERM numbers.  Automate this as a regression test.
7. Freeze the software stack in environment.yml (CUDA 11.8 wheels) so installation matches the hardware used in the paper.
8. Release pretrained checkpoints and scripts that reproduce Tables 1–3 with a single command.

The manuscript presents a very detailed experimental plan and expected numbers, but the artefact that was actually executed cannot reproduce (or even start) the experiments.  

Key inconsistencies / blockers
1. Missing module:  src.autospu  –  the main training script crashes immediately, so none of the promised unit-tests, sanity checks or benchmarks are run.  All reported figures are therefore hypothetical and unsupported by logs.
2. Absence of real results: the only console output is the package-installation log followed by the import error.  No CSV/JSON metrics, plots or checkpoints exist, so none of the claims (e.g.
   • WG-Acc 92 % on Waterbirds
   • mCE 0.63 on CIFAR10-C
   • Δlogits ≈0.05 after swapping)
   are empirically demonstrated.
3. Environment drift: requirements.txt installs PyTorch 2.8 + CUDA 12.8 wheels (>3 GB). The text, however, specifies CUDA 11.8 and PyTorch ≤2.4. This mismatch both inflates install time and risks further incompatibilities (e.g. segment_anything pre-built extensions).
4. CI philosophy vs. reality: the plan emphasises unit tests and regression guards, yet pytest is never invoked because the main script crashes first.  Even if the import were fixed, the tests live in tests/test_autospu.py but the missing autospu implementation would still make them fail.
5. Dataset policy conflict: main.py deliberately aborts if the Waterbirds images are not pre-downloaded, but the instructions also disable automatic downloads.  In a clean evaluation sandbox this guarantees failure.

Actionable steps to reach a high consistency score
A. Ship the missing implementation modules (autospu.py, fourier.py, mask_bank.py, etc.) and ensure they can run in **CPU-only** mode so reviewers without GPUs can still execute the sanity experiment.
B. Add a lightweight smoke test to the default run (e.g. 16 synthetic 32×32 RGB images) so that the pipeline finishes end-to-end in <30 s and writes a metrics JSON.  This proves that every loss term and log writer is functional.
C. Pin the environment to the versions you actually tested (e.g. torch==2.2.0+cu118, torchvision==0.17.0, timm==0.9.12) and move heavy CUDA libraries behind an `extra-cuda.txt` optional file.
D. Make data access graceful: if Waterbirds is absent, fall back to a  small dummy dataset and still run unit tests; print a warning rather than aborting.
E. Produce and include real numbers: run Experiment 1 locally, commit the resulting CSV/plot, and reference its checksum in the paper.  Reviewers can then verify that re-running reproduces the same numbers within tolerance.
F. Ensure pytest is called in main CI (e.g. `python -m pytest -q && python -m src.main`) so that a missing component is caught early.
G. Provide a `README.md` with a one-line command to reproduce Experiment 1 on CPU and Experiment 2 on a single GPU, including expected wall-clock times.

By implementing A–G you will turn the paper from a well-written proposal into a reproducible, self-consistent study that justifies the strong performance claims.

1. Claims vs. Evidence – The manuscript claims ≥92 % worst-group accuracy on Waterbirds and broad OOD improvements, yet the only numbers produced in the attached run are:
   • Smoke-test FakeData val-acc 25 %
   • Waterbirds *fallback* subset val-acc 40 %
   No baseline or AutoSpuSwap-off comparison is reported, and neither metric approaches the advertised figures.  Thus the current results cannot substantiate any robustness claim.

2. Missing full experiments – EXP-2 and EXP-3 are reduced to two epochs on a toy subset and are therefore unable to reveal the method’s effect.  Run the full 30-epoch Waterbirds training and the shift-suite when the real datasets are present, or at least ship the corresponding result CSVs so the paper’s tables can be verified off-line.

3. Baseline absence – The logs contain no ERM / GroupDRO / DFR numbers, so consistency across methods cannot be assessed.  Always output the complete table (mean ± std over seeds) even when fall-back data are used; this will expose trend consistency even if the absolute values differ.

4. Internal sanity checks – Unit tests only assert that context-swap changes > 90 % of pixels, not that it preserves label semantics or improves invariance.  Add simple automated checks such as:
   • Δlogits(orig, cf) for ERM vs. AutoSpuSwap (should shrink)
   • WG-Acc gap between swap_prob = 1.0 and swap_prob = 0 (should widen)
This would provide quantitative evidence that each component works as intended.

5. Fallback vs. headline – Graceful degradation is useful for CI, but reviewers need one canonical, fully reproducible path that reaches the headline numbers.  Provide a cached result file (or quick-download model weights) so the exact 92 % WG-Acc can be re-evaluated without a multi-hour GPU run.

6. Statistical soundness – Only a single seed is executed.  Report ≥3 seeds and include paired t-tests (already claimed in text) inside the logged output to demonstrate significance.

7. Resource / environment parity – The run installs CUDA wheels but executes on CPU; this bloats installation time and may mask GPU-specific defects.  Gate CUDA installs behind a GPU check or provide a separate cpu-requirements.txt.

Actionable next steps to reach a consistency score ≥8:
   a. Ship full Waterbirds, CIFAR10-C, MetaShift, PACS results (mean ± std) with code that reproduces them end-to-end.
   b. Always log baselines alongside AutoSpuSwap in the same run script.
   c. Add automatic invariance diagnostics (Δlogits, PGD robustness) to the standard evaluation.
   d. Run ≥3 seeds, compute confidence intervals and p-values in the result CSV.
   e. Provide lightweight pre-computed checkpoints for quick verification.
   f. Separate CI smoke test from scientific benchmark scripts to avoid confusion between toy and real results.

Major blocking issues prevent the experiments from producing any numerical evidence, so the current results cannot support the stated scientific claims.

1. Code fails before training
   • The Waterbirds run crashes inside get_train_loader → torch.utils.data.DataLoader with an illegal kw-arg `split`.  The WILDS 2.0 helper removed this argument; your wrapper (`get_waterbirds_loaders`) therefore breaks with the newest WILDS release.
   • Because the very first experiment aborts, none of the promised CSVs, t-tests, or diagnostic figures are generated.  All headline numbers (≥92 % WG-Acc, mCE 0.62, etc.) remain hypothetical.

2. Mismatch between narrative and execution
   • The paper-style description claims three completed experiments with 5 + 3 seeds, yet the log shows only package installation and the fatal exception.  No seed loop, no baseline models, no ablation – so there is no way to verify trends or internal coherence.
   • Many implementation details (e.g. SAM integration, last-layer DFR step, Fourier perturbation weights) are referenced in the text but are either stubbed (DummyMaskBank) or entirely absent from the executed code path.

3. Environment drift
   • You allow very wide version ranges (torch 2.2-2.8, wilds 2.x, etc.).  API changes across these spans are large.  Pin exact versions that you have tested (e.g. torch==2.2.2, wilds==2.0.0, torchvision==0.17.2).  Put them in requirements.txt or a conda-lock file and CI.
   • Run a minimal smoke test in CI that actually instantiates the loaders and one training step to catch such incompatibilities.

4. Missing real results & sanity checks
   • Until real metrics are saved to disk, all statistics in the manuscript are unverifiable.  Add unit tests that parse the output CSV and assert that mean WG-Acc > 90 %, ID-Acc drop < 1 pp, etc.  CI should fail if they are absent.
   • Store one reference result file in the repo so reviewers can instantly compare hashes.

5. Suggested concrete fixes to reach a high consistency score
   a. Pin and document library versions; freeze them in a Dockerfile.
   b. Patch get_waterbirds_loaders: drop the unsupported ‘split’ kw-arg or vendor-lock an older WILDS helper.
   c. Replace DummyMaskBank with real SAM-based masks or, at minimum, keep a pre-computed mask cache so the advertised pipeline actually runs.
   d. Run the full 30-epoch Waterbirds training in CI on a small image subset (e.g. 128 samples) to ensure end-to-end success; on full data only in manual/ GPU workflow.
   e. Commit at least one completed result CSV (5 seeds) and the accompanying paired t-test script; make the paper tables pull directly from this file.
   f. Provide real ablation toggles via command line rather than duplicated ‘swap0’ branches, reducing code divergence and testing burden.

Once the code executes and produces verifiable numbers that match the written claims, the internal coherence will improve dramatically and the work could reach a consistency score in the 8-10 range.

The conceptual design of AutoSpuSwap is carefully thought-out, but the implementation that was actually executed is not yet able to generate any numbers.  The run aborts on the very first mini-batch with
```
TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not str
```
This indicates that the training loop is assuming the WILDS dataloader yields a dict (batch["images"]).  In reality it is yielding a tuple/list, so the helper you already wrote ( _parse_batch ) is never called.  Because the code crashes before an epoch finishes:
• No Waterbirds accuracy numbers are produced
• Subsequent CI checks (Δ-logits, PGD, shift-suite, etc.) are never reached
• The stated claims (≥92 % WG-Acc, mCE ↓, …) therefore have no supporting evidence

Key actionable fixes to reach a high consistency score:
1. Unify batch parsing
   • Replace the three manual indexing lines in run_waterbirds() with
     ```python
     x_raw, y_raw, meta_raw, idx_raw = _parse_batch(raw_batch)
     ```
   • Do the same for the validation loop and anywhere else a batch is unpacked.
   • Keep the _parse_batch() helper at the top level so every experiment calls it.
2. Add a minimal unit test that loads one batch from each split and passes it through _parse_batch() so CI catches this class of bug immediately.
3. Verify WILDS version compatibility
   • You hard-code Waterbirds version 1.0 in config.yml but the narrative and EXP-1 header still say “v2.0”.  Stick to one version and delete the other from the text and code comments.
4. Smoke-test forward/backward *with each loss* in CI
   • Run one step of ERM and one step of AutoSpuSwap inside tests/smoke.py; assert loss.isfinite().  This would have caught the crash before the full run started.
5. Tighten the mask pipeline
   • Assert that len(mask_bank)==len(dataset) and that masks have exactly two unique values {0,1}.  Emit a warning if not.
6. Re-run and commit the resulting CSVs plus stderr/stdout logs so reviewers can see the numeric evidence.
7. (Optional) Downgrade to a smaller Torch build (CPU-only or CUDA 11.8) in CI to keep wheel download size reasonable; it currently spends several minutes fetching large nvidia-cu12 packages even though the GitHub runner has no GPU.

Once the code executes end-to-end and produces the claimed numbers, the design should easily score in the 7-9 range because:
• The ablation plan is thorough and causal (swap0, Fourier-off, etc.)
• Statistical tests and CI thresholds are pre-registered
• Multi-shift evaluation (corruption, natural, context) is included.

But until the runtime errors are fixed, the experiment cannot support any scientific claim.
